chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Yahya, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

I heard Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Quran was revealed in three parts: one-third is regarding us and our enemies, one-third is about Sunnah and examples, and one-third is about Impositions and regulations.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: How is the Quran divided into three parts according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the tripartite structure of the Quran, emphasizing the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt as a primary subject of revelation alongside legal injunctions and moral parables. In Shia scholarship, this division underscores the Quran's dual role as a source of jurisprudence (fara'id) and a guide for spiritual and historical identity, linking divine law directly to the Imams. The narration serves to validate the Ahl al-Bayt's central position in Islamic exegesis and governance.
